==English== {{Chess diagram |tright | | | | | |kd| | | | | |pd| | | | | | | | |pd| | | | | | | |ua| | | | | | | |pl|kl| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |The only way for white to [[draw]] is to play d5 to '''fix''' (sense 2.2) black's pawns.}} ===Alternative forms=== * {{alt|en|fixe||verb|archaic}} ===Etymology=== {{root|en|ine-pro|*dʰeygʷ-}} From {{inh|en|enm|fixen}}, borrowed from {{der|en|fro|*fixer}} (attested only as {{m|fro|ficher}}, {{m|fro|fichier}}; > English {{m|en|fitch}}), from {{m|fro|fix||fastened; fixed}}, from {{der|en|la|fīxus||immovable; steady; stable; fixed}}, from {{m|la|fīgō||to drive in; stick; fasten}}, from {{der|en|ine-pro|*dʰeygʷ-||to jab; stick; set}}. Related to {{m|en|dig}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/fɪks/|a=UK,US,CA,AU}} ** {{audio|en|en-us-fix.ogg|a=US}} * {{IPA|en|/fəks/|a=NZ}} * {{rhymes|en|ɪks|s=1}} * {{hyph|en|fix}} ===Verb=== {{wikidata lexeme|L178}} {{en-verb|~es|~ing|~t,~ed}} # {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[pierce]]; now generally replaced by [[transfix]]. ## {{lb|en|transitive|by extension}} (Of a piercing look) to direct at someone. ##: {{ux|en|He '''fixed''' me with a sickly grin, and said, "I told you it wouldn't work!"}} ##* {{RQ:Lindsay Redheap|page=111|passage=She sniffed, too, comprehendingly, and '''fixed''' her son with a relentless eye.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[attach]]; to [[affix]]; to hold [[in place]] or at a particular [[time]]. #: {{ux|en|A dab of chewing gum will '''fix''' your note to the bulletin board.}} #: {{ux|en|A leech can '''fix''' itself to your skin without you feeling it.}} #: {{ux|en|The Constitution '''fixes''' the date when Congress must meet.}} #* {{quote-video game|en|developer={{w|DICE (company)|DICE}}|title=w:Battlefield 1|genre=[[historical fiction|Historical Fiction]]|location=w:Stockholm|publisher=w:Electronic Arts|year=2016|system=PC, Xbox One, Playstation 4|scene=American Ballroom Blitz Pre-Battle Speech (Operations)|note=set in '''1918''' during [[World War I]]|passage=We've come a long, long way boys! Now it's time for America to show its teeth. '''Fix''' bayonets!}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|figuratively|usually in the passive}} To focus or determine (oneself, on a concept); to [[fixate]]. ##: {{ux|en|She's '''fixed''' on the idea of becoming a doctor.}} ## {{lb|en|transitive|chess}} To prevent enemy [[pawn]]s from [[advance|advancing]] by directly [[oppose|opposing]] the most advanced one with one of one's own pawns so as to [[threaten]] to [[capture]] any advancing [[backward pawn]]s. # {{senseid|en|repair}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To [[mend]], to [[repair]]. #: {{ux|en|That heater will start a fire if you don't '''fix''' it.}} #: {{ux|en|You can't '''fix''' stupid.}} #: {{ux|en|'''Fix''' this for me.}} ## {{lb|en|hyperbolic|chiefly|with|{{m|en|would}}}} To be [[immensely]] [[pleasurable]] to. ##: {{ux|en|Some pizza rolls would '''fix''' me right now.}} ##: {{ux|en|Getting tongued by a hot woman would '''fix''' me.}} # {{lb|en|ditransitive|informal}} To prepare (food or drink). #: {{ux|en|She '''fixed''' dinner for the kids.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1945|author=Marianne Steiff Finton Meisel|title=Years Before the Flood|page=14 |passage=She '''fixed''' Peter a slice of black bread and jam by cutting the hard crust petalwise around the edge, so the child could tear off convenient pieces.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=2013|author=w:Iris Smyles|title=Iris Has Free Time|location=Berkeley, CA|publisher={{w|Counterpoint (publisher)|Counterpoint}}|isbn=9781593765194|page={{gbooks|M2yDAgAAQBAJ|94|fixed}}|passage=I '''fixed''' us drinks—orange juice with some vodka I'd gotten on sale—and washed a few dishes to get my mind off Jess and the fact of his not texting back.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To make (a contest, vote, or gamble) unfair; to [[privilege]] one contestant or a particular group of contestants, usually before the contest begins; to arrange immunity for defendants by tampering with the justice system via bribery or extortion.Sutherland, Edwin H. (ed) (1937): The Professional Thief: by a Professional Thief. Chicago: University of Chicago Press. [Reprinted by various publishers in subsequent decades.] #: {{ux|en|A majority of voters believed the election was '''fixed''' in favor of the incumbent.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|US|informal}} To [[surgical]]ly [[render]] an animal, especially a pet, [[infertile]]. #: {{ux|en|Rover stopped digging under the fence after we had the vet '''fix''' him.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|mathematics|semantics}} To [[map]] (a [[point]] or [[subset]]) to [[itself]]. #: {{ux|en|The function f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R} ; f(x) := 4x - 3 '''fixes''' the point 1 \in \mathbb{R}, since f(1) = 4(1) - 3 = 1.}} # {{lb|en|transitive|informal}} To take revenge on, to best; to serve justice on an assumed miscreant. #: {{ux|en|He got caught breaking into lockers, so a couple of guys '''fixed''' him after work.}} # {{senseid|en|photography}}{{lb|en|transitive}} To render (a photographic impression) permanent by treating with such applications as will make it insensitive to the action of light. # {{senseid|en|transitive chemistry}}{{lb|en|transitive|chemistry|biology}} To convert into a stable or available form. #: {{ux|en|Legumes are valued in crop rotation for their ability to '''fix''' nitrogen.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1878|author=w:William de Wiveleslie Abney|title=A treatise on photography |passage=it is well to '''fix''' with sodium hyposulphite , and to wash as usual}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To [[become]] [[fixed]]; to [[settle]] or [[remain]] [[permanently]]; to cease from wandering; to rest. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1665|author=w:Edmund Waller|title=Upon Her Maiesties New Buildings at Somerset-House |passage=Accuſing ſome malignant Star,
Not ''Britain'', for that fateful War,
Your kindneſs baniſhes your fear,
Reſolv’d to '''fix''' for ever here.}} #* {{RQ:Southey Thalaba|||A cheerless place! the solitary Bee,
Whose buzzing was the only sound of life,
Flew there on restless wing,
Seeking in vain one blossom, where to '''fix'''.}} # {{lb|en|intransitive}} To become firm, so as to resist [[volatilization]]; to cease to flow or be fluid; to [[congeal]]; to become hard and [[malleable]], as a metallic substance. #* {{RQ:Bacon Sylva Sylvarum|passage=quicksilver will '''fix''', so asto endure the hammer}} # {{senseid|en|inject}} {{lb|en|slang|intransitive}} To [[shoot]] up; to [[inject]] a [[drug]]. #* {{RQ:William Burroughs Junkie|passage=She doesn't have to worry about stool pigeons because every law in the Federal District knows that Lupita sells junk. She keeps outfits in glasses of alcohol so the junkies can '''fix''' in the joint and walk out clean.}} # {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[arrange]] (an event etc.). #: {{ux|en|Could you '''fix''' it for me
